A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FLAME, with readable text, equations, tables, and figures. Corresponding methods and experiments can be reliably matched. v1 ends with references; v3 includes supplementary Sections A–D, including material relocated from the main text.

before.justification: v1 reports original FLAME retrieval and classification results, prompt and backbone ablations, and computational-cost measurements in Tables 1–7 and Figures 4–5.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds retrieval benchmarks, compositionality and few-shot evaluations, semantic-level ablations, and scalability results.

M1.justification: The original contrastive training, multifaceted prompts, facet-decoupled attention, and offline embeddings remain unchanged. Sections 4.4 and C.3 add a limited inference extension: mapping image patches into vocabulary words and feeding these representations with examples into the frozen LLM for few-shot prediction.

E1.justification: v3 adds DCI and DOCCI-test long-context retrieval in Table 1, Winoground and SugarCrepe compositionality in C.2, and MiniImageNet few-shot image comprehension in C.3. These substantially broaden evaluated task requirements. CC3M/YFCC15M training and the original retrieval and classification coverage remain.

E2.justification: Table C4 introduces reported comparisons against Frozen, LQAE, V2L-Tokenizer, and SPAE for few-shot image comprehension, adding a distinct family of comparison methods. Existing comparator memberships remain unchanged; extending CLIP and Long-CLIP to DCI/DOCCI alone does not change that comparator set.

E3.justification: New evaluations introduce 2-way/5-way, 1-shot/3-shot in-context prediction and repetition conditions, plus compositionality scoring. Appendix C.5 extends ViT-L/14 evaluation to YFCC15M and large-model multilingual comparisons. Original training settings remain unchanged; newly supplied hyperparameters and long-text scoring details are disclosures rather than demonstrated protocol revisions.

E4.justification: v3 adds semantic-level ablations (Table C7), patch-to-word interpretability examples (Figure 5), and Urban-1k retrieval case studies (Figure D2). It also extends backbone scalability analyses to YFCC15M (Tables C5, C6, C8). The original prompt-count and backbone ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, independent-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Table C4 introduces repetition settings within the few-shot evaluation, without identifying them as statistical replications or providing uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial results for the new benchmarks, semantic-level ablations, and larger models; Table C4 reports FLAME averages of 86.8% and 68.4% for 2-way and 5-way comprehension. Tables 2–7 remain numerically unchanged. Reported online-training time changes from 184.7 hours in v1 Figure 5 to 1084.7 hours in v3 Figure 6, without explanation.

T1.justification: Sections 4.4 and C.3 add mathematical definitions for patch-to-word mapping and the construction of in-context examples and predictions. The original contrastive objective and attention formulation remain unchanged, and no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about frozen LLMs, multifaceted prompting, efficiency, long-context understanding, and multilingual generalization. The headline numerical gains also remain unchanged; additional evaluations support and extend applications of the retained contribution.

C2.justification: v3 interprets vocabulary mappings as semantic interpretability and semantic-level ablations as supporting prompt generalizability without detrimental caption-prompt misalignment. It removes v1's detailed saturation explanation for excessive prompts while retaining the performance-plateau observation and computational-overhead limitation.

D1.justification: Appendices A–B supply previously missing optimizer, batch-size, learning-rate, warmup, and complete prompt details, including default selections. Section 4.1 additionally specifies caption-generation prompts and long-text similarity aggregation. Conversely, v3 removes several exact checkpoint links and Long-CLIP/DreamLIP code footnotes; FLAME's code URL remains.

R1.justification: The principal related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain stable. v3 adds focused references connecting semantic decomposition to scene-graph research and DOCCI, alongside citations for compositionality benchmarks, AdamW, and frozen-LLM visual-comprehension comparators.

P1.justification: Most main-text wording and narrative organization are retained. v3 adds a semantic-interpretability subsection and an organized A–D supplement, renumbers the ablation subsection, adds acknowledgements, updates contact information, and makes localized explanatory and shortening edits.

P2.justification: v3 adds interpretability and retrieval-example figures and multiple supplementary tables, expands Table 1, and substantially redistributes displays. The original multilingual Figure 4 is split between the main text and Figure C1. Figure 3 highlights extracted features, and the runtime plot's vertical scale changes.

improvement.justification: v3 resolves an important reproducibility deficiency by supplying the full prompts and training settings that the supplied v1 references but omits. Semantic-level ablations and new compositionality, few-shot, and scaling evaluations substantially strengthen scrutiny of the claimed capabilities. Removed checkpoint links and the unexplained runtime revision are drawbacks, but the gains in reproducibility and evidential support outweigh them.
